parallel.requirements: The run recognized a clean-room reverse-engineering task for a Lua 5.5.1 interpreter, with source lookup, wrapping, and binary analysis prohibited.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent used swarm mode, delegated nine broad behavioral specification workstreams to children, and kept implementation and final assembly in the parent trajectory.
parallel.implementation: After gathering child specifications, the parent began a C interpreter under src, including core/value/AST/parser pieces, but did not complete runtime, standard library, build, or deliverable integration.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The packed artifact contained partial src files, multiple specs, README, .git metadata, and the original executable, but no evaluator-usable replacement executable.
parallel.verification: Parallel work included many probes against the original binary and some partial command execution, but no integrated replacement build or evaluator-aligned verification succeeded.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The attempt timed out with an artifact marked not ok and an official compile_failed result, leaving all 1387 tests not run.

serial.requirements: The serial run faced the same clean-room Lua interpreter prompt and accepted observation of the provided binary as the only behavioral source.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial actor did not delegate; it sequentially probed behavior itself and retained all research, implementation, and closure decisions locally.
serial.implementation: The serial trajectory focused on detailed behavior discovery, especially numeric formatting and global declaration semantics, but did not add replacement interpreter source.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact contained README, .git metadata, and the original executable, with no new source tree or compiled replacement deliverable.
serial.verification: Serial verification was behavioral probing of the original binary rather than testing a replacement implementation, so it never established deliverable compatibility.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run also timed out and failed official evaluation at compile time, with all 1387 tests not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room obligation to implement a Lua-compatible executable only from binary observations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the identical prompt and also treated the binary as the behavioral source.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement interpretation difference is visible; the divergence is in execution strategy rather than the stated task target.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used swarm mode with nine direct child agents while the parent remained the apparent implementation owner.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial protocol validation shows no delegation, no subagents, and no parallel execution.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposed behavioral research across children; serial kept the entire investigation and any implementation obligation in one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were scoped as behavioral specifications such as core language, errors, strings, and libraries, not separately owned interoperating implementation components.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept findings in one main context and performed direct probes without cross-agent handoff boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced handoff surfaces for spec findings, but no proven missing requirement or incompatible component contract; serial avoided those surfaces by design.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created partial C source files and specification files in the submitted artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered no replacement source tree; its artifact only included README, .git metadata, and the original executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel advanced from probing into partial implementation, while serial stayed almost entirely in discovery mode.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spawned children and later had child/spec uptake observed, but parent closure happened before a complete usable implementation lifecycle.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle to join or inspect; all work remained in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel needed to manage child results and parent implementation timing; serial had no lifecycle boundary beyond its own unfinished probing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children shared temporary paths, and agent-3 wrote /tmp/t4.lua that agent-1 later consumed after it had been clobbered.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had a single actor and no concurrent child sharing of temporary probe fixtures.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete shared-environment contamination episode; serial did not expose the same concurrent temp-file hazard.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel probes produced behavior notes, but the official completed evaluation reports compile_failed and no tests run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial probes did not become replacement verification; the official completed evaluation also reports compile_failed and no tests run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither run reached evaluator-aligned acceptance of a replacement executable; there is no verification-based outcome split.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after a high-token, high-tool-call swarm run and closed with partial files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out but with far fewer requests and tool calls, closing after probing rather than implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the time budget, but parallel spent it across many agents and partial source creation whereas serial spent it in one extended probe sequence.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations failed at compile time with zero passed tests and all 1387 tests not run. The material trajectory difference is that parallel used nine delegated behavioral probes and produced partial C source plus specs, while serial stayed single-actor and produced no replacement implementation. The retained artifact-leakage episode is an adverse parallel process event, but it does not explain a discordant official outcome because there is no discordance.
parallel_contributors: Delegated research produced specs and a partial source tree but no complete evaluator-usable replacement executable.
A shared temporary probe fixture was clobbered across children, causing local rework during behavior discovery.
serial_contributors: Single-actor probing avoided child coordination hazards but did not progress to replacement implementation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel left incomplete interpreter source files; serial left no replacement source files.
Both failures are ultimately compile-level delivery failures rather than demonstrated semantic mismatches.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator stopped at compile_failed in both modes, so no behavioral tests ran in either trajectory.

candidates.reason: The parent took implementation ownership and edited source files; the defect is incompletion, not absence of an implementation owner.
Children produced specifications rather than independently owned implementation components requiring integration.
The parent was the only actor editing source and packaging artifacts; final assembly was unfinished rather than ownerless.
No separately assigned pipeline stages lacked an end-to-end owner; the parent remained responsible for build and delivery.
Parallel did not block productive implementation behind one mandatory serial preflight; research and implementation overlapped enough to reject this gate.
The child investigations overlapped and the parent began implementation before all work was simply serialized into a completed first phase.
Although the parallel run was broad, the evidence does not isolate a displaced critical path better than ordinary unfinished implementation.
High fan-out and timeout are visible, but the required separate budget-exhaustion episode displacing indispensable work is not directly proven.
Several child scopes were broad, but no single child assignment is proven to be the dominant overbroad blocker for the final deliverable.
The delegated children received explicit behavioral research scopes and clean-room constraints; no known required task fact was omitted from a child brief and followed into unusable work.
The children were not assigned separately owned implementation components expected to interoperate, so no missing component interface contract materialized.
No specific known finding is shown to disappear during transfer and force the parent to repeat work without it.
Large specification material existed, but no returned handoff is proven too large or insufficiently structured to consume within a decision window.
No parent action is shown consuming a child report that described a superseded workspace or requirement state.
No incompatible returned reports or contracts are visible at a parent decision point and left unadjudicated.
The parent did not make a supported whole-task completion claim with a visible unresolved integrated gap; the run simply timed out with incomplete work.
No replacement or retry agent repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints as an independent episode.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The retained killed task was a local probe subprocess after temp contamination, not parent cancellation of a needed child result.
No complete promotable interpreter or compatible component set existed before closure; partial modules do not satisfy this label.
There is no completed integrated verification followed by a later child merge without post-merge checks.
Children produced behavioral specs, not completed delegated implementation that the parent failed to retrieve and integrate.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that remained trapped below the parent before closure.
No required child failure was abandoned without parent takeover; the observable adverse episode is temp-file contamination handled by rerunning probes.
No concrete completed child result is shown available to the parent and then ignored while the parent proceeded inconsistently.
The parent and children were actively probing and editing; timeout alone does not prove blind waiting over available progress.
No concurrent agents wrote different implementation paths claiming overlapping behavior or build ownership that required reconciliation.
The observed same path was a temporary probe file in /tmp, not a source or configuration file edited under implementation ownership.
No non-entry library, module, or configuration source produced by another agent was replaced or recreated.
No required executable or submitted entry-point artifact was overwritten while another agent owned or used it.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current final-tree outputs or invalidated provenance.
Shared workspace risk exists, but the material realized problem is specifically temporary artifact leakage rather than unspecific workspace write instability.
One child wrote /tmp/t4.lua as a probe fixture and another child later consumed that shared path as stable input, discovered it had been clobbered, and reran missing probes with unique paths.
candidates.realized_consequence: The contaminated temp fixture caused a hung probe to be killed and forced duplicate probing under /tmp/errs_t4.lua, wasting time and destabilizing the child evidence stream.
candidates.near_match_reason: The leaked object was an auxiliary /tmp probe fixture, not source, configuration, or a submitted deliverable under same-file edit ownership.
